questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: A good academic/career opportunity combined with a good location in the US to explore nearby cities and Canada.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: I found it quite easy. I received the information on email from Dartmouth that I needed in good time. There was a quick response time on emails when I asked questions.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: There was a introduction meeting with the exchange counselor and she showed us around campus. That was all. I was expecting a bit more than that and maybe some social events. The very limited introduction made the first few weeks a bit harder than expected because it took some time to find your way around campus and the social life there.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: When arriving in Winter term at least, there was not a lot of effort from Dartmouth to help you integrate on campus and get to know people. You have to do it all on your own and maybe get a bit out of your comfort zone and show up for clubs, events etc. I think this experience can be different if your arrive in Fall term where the new class arrives.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing through my host institution

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: On campus

questions.question: What options were available for on campus housing? *
questions.answer: You cannot choose your accommodation and have to live on campus. However, I think the best option is to live on campus anyways. You can indicate your preferences when applying for accommodation and I think they try to find something that fits those. The accommodation varies on quality but I was happy with mine. I was living in a three room - three people type of accommodation. Be prepared to have roomies. I found this to be nice because it made it easier to get to know some people.

questions.question: What options were available for meal plans or cooking facilities? *
questions.answer: You will automatically be enrolled in the meal plan. I was a bit worried about this before arriving. But the food was fine and it was easy to get a healthy meal. There is a lot of different food to choose from.

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about on campus housing? *
questions.answer: I will recommend to choose roomies when applying. I made some good friends through mine. But also be aware that you can get a type of accommodation where you live two people in one room. So have that in mind when you choose whether you want roomies or not.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The houses are a bit old. Dont expect newly build and modern housing.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I found it quite easy. I had no problems.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: You have to apply and they will send this information to your email. Then you fill it out and they send you a admission letter. After that they will send you information about where to apply for housing and courses.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: If you are unsure about anything I will recommend to reach out to the exchange counselor (mine was Noelle). She was very quick to respond and very helpful.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: I got 5/6 courses that I wanted. In winter term I got all the classes that I applied for. In spring term I got 2/3. If you dont get your courses you can apply for all of the remaining with free spots. This is first come, first serve. So be quick to register for these courses if you dont get the ones you applied for in the first round.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: You need to get overwrites for the prerequisites for the courses because you dont have a record with Dartmouth. You can contact the registrars office for help with this.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: I liked all of my courses. The professors was very good and welcoming.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Did you take BA or MA courses at your host university? *
questions.answer: Both

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: The level was kind of the same compared to back home. The exams was easier but there was more graded work during the term.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: There is a lot of graded assignments during the term and you get grades for participation.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer:
Environmental Economics and Governance. 
Theory of Finance. 
Financial Accounting. 
International Finance and Open-economy macroeconomics. 
Economics of Governments and Public Policy. 
Business Management and Strategy.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer:
The courses on TUCK. The work load was not to high and the professors was very passionate. 
I also really enjoyed International Finance and Open-economy macroeconomics (ECON29).

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None. I think the prices that Dartmouth shows on their website was quite accurate.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer:
Dartmouth had almost all of the books in an online version in their library. I was able to get a good and cheap phone subscription on Mint Mobile. 
My personal spending was quite low since food, housing etc was already paid for and the gym was free to use. The transportation on the area is free with your student card. 

I didn't include the costs of my travels in this.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: There is a lot of clubs and events going on all the time. They are easy to find (sign up for the listserv) and very accessible.

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: All kinds of clubs you could think of. Outdoor clubs (cycling, hiking, shooting), dance clubs, knitting clubs, political clubs etc. Dartmouth also has skiway you can use in the winter.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: The outdoor club activities. I found that people that showed up for this was very welcoming and nice. It is a nice way to make friends while also exploring the nature outside campus.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: I went to Boston, New York City, roadtrip to Canada (Montreal) and Miami. I recommend all of these trips. The winter is very cold there so going somewhere hot like Miami for spring break was very nice if you are there for both winter and spring break.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Pretty easy. It took a 2-3 weeks to get to know people, figure out the meal plan, getting used the structure of the classes there and how everything worked grade wise. But after that there was no problems adjusting.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: The clubs and especially the outdoor club is a great place to get to know people.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: No.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: I enjoyed that something was always going on. You could always find an event, club meeting or something the like if you felt like it. The greek life (sororities and fraternities) was a big thing and a lot of things was happening there in the weekends. It is a very social experience and I was always hanging out with my friends which I really enjoyed.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Be prepared that the introduction when arriving is very limited. 

There was not a lot of exchange students (maybe 12-15) when I got there. You are only going to be 1-2 from KU. 

Be aware that the academic level is not low. So you have to work for it while being there.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: See the above.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Meeting a lot of new friends, traveling around the US and experiencing the great courses/academics.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: The first few weeks. It took some time to find your way around, get to know people, find your classrooms, figure out how the meal plan worked etc. Also, it was minus 15 degrees when I got there so not a lot of things was happening on campus. Therefore, the first few weeks was a bit of a challenges. But after that it was a great experience!

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
